say: You give it a complex number, $z = a + bi$. It gives back the **conjugate**, $\bar z = a - bi$.
The key idea: only the sign of the $i$ part flips. The real part stays the same, and $z\bar z$ is always a real number.

how.higher: Higher level uses it as a step inside bigger parts, in 2015, 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2025, mostly to divide complex numbers or plot a conjugate. It is never the main skill.
how.ordinary: Ordinary level uses it every year from 2015 to 2025, nearly always as the first move when dividing complex numbers, or when plotting $\bar z$ on an Argand diagram. It is the main skill of one part, in 2022.

example.question: Let $z = 4 - 3i$. Write down $\bar z$ and find $z\bar z$.

steps.title: Write the conjugate
steps.say: Keep the real part and flip the sign of the $i$ part. $z = 4 - 3i$ becomes $\hl{1}{\bar z}$.

steps.title: Multiply z by its conjugate
steps.say: Now multiply $z$ by $\hl{1}{\bar z}$. Expand the two brackets.

steps.title: Simplify
steps.say: With $i^2 = -1$, the last term becomes $+9$. The answer has no $i$ in it.

higher.tip: Show the multiplication of top and bottom by the conjugate. It is a step of its own in the scheme.

ordinary.tip: Write the conjugate down. 'Conjugate identified' earns partial credit before any multiplying.
Multiply top and bottom by the same number. That earns marks even if you picked the wrong conjugate.

sources.quote: same number, even if incorrect conjugate

ordinary.tip: Finish in the form $a + bi$. A single fraction like $\frac{15 - 30i}{5}$ loses a mark.

ordinary.tip: Label every point you plot, including $\bar z$. Missing labels cost a mark.

say: You give it a power of $i$, $i^n$. It gives back one of four values: $1$, $i$, $-1$ or $-i$.
The key idea: the powers repeat in a cycle of four, and $i^4 = 1$. Divide $n$ by $4$ and only the remainder matters.

how.higher: Higher level uses it only as a step inside longer complex-number parts, in 2020, 2022 and 2023, usually as $i^2 = -1$ while expanding brackets.
how.ordinary: Ordinary level used it once, in 2019 on Paper 1 Q2(b), as $i^2 = -1$ when substituting $2 + i$ into a quadratic.

steps.title: Split off fours
steps.say: The powers of $i$ repeat every four, because $i^4 = 1$. Divide $23$ by $4$: it goes in $5$ times with remainder $3$.

steps.title: Use i to the four is one
steps.say: Replace $i^4$ with $1$. Any power of $1$ is $1$, so only $i^3$ is left.

higher.tip: Watch the sign when $i^2$ appears. Mishandling $-2i^2$ costs a mark even if the rest is right.

ordinary.tip: When you test a value, finish with a conclusion. Not drawing one is treated as an error.

say: You give it a complex number, $z$. It gives back a **point** on the Argand diagram, $(\text{Re}, \text{Im})$.
The key idea: the real part is the $x$ value and the imaginary part is the $y$ value. So $3 - 2i$ is the point $(3, -2)$.

how.higher: Higher level asks for it in 2023 and 2024 as part of a Paper 1 question: plotting $u$ and its conjugate in 2023, and plotting $u$ in polar form in 2024. In 2024 it is the main skill, inside a 15-mark part.
how.ordinary: Ordinary level asks for it every year from 2015 to 2025 except 2018, always as the main skill: plot two or three numbers, label them, then use the points for a modulus or a sum.

example.question: Let $z = -2 + 3i$ and $w = 4 - i$. Find $z + w$. Plot $z$, $w$ and $z + w$ on an Argand diagram and label each point.

steps.title: Read each number as a point
steps.say: The real part is the $x$ value. The imaginary part is the $y$ value.

steps.title: Add the numbers
steps.say: Add the real parts together, then the imaginary parts. Call the answer $\hl{1}{z + w}$.

steps.title: Plot and label
steps.say: Mark the points $(-2, 3)$, $(4, -1)$ and $(2, 2)$. Count along the Re axis first, then up the Im axis.

lines.text: Label them $z$, $w$ and $z + w$. Unlabelled points lose a mark.

higher.tip: Label the point you plot. An otherwise correct diagram without labels loses a mark.
Plot as accurately as you can. The scheme accepts a small tolerance on each coordinate.

ordinary.tip: Label every point. Correct points with no or wrong labels lose a mark.

say: You give it two complex numbers, $a + bi$ and $c + di$. It gives back one answer in the form $a + bi$.
The key idea: treat $i$ like a letter and expand as normal. Then replace every $i^2$ with $-1$.

how.higher: Higher level uses it as a working step in 2015, 2016, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025, and as the main skill in 2022 Q3(a)(i) and 2023 Q4(a), worth 5 marks.
how.ordinary: Ordinary level asks for it as the main skill in 2016 to 2023, usually 5 to 10 marks inside Q1 to Q3: substitute into an expression such as $z_1 z_2 - 2z_1$ and simplify.

example.question: Let $z_1 = 2 + i$ and $z_2 = 3 - 2i$. Find $z_1 z_2 - 2z_1$. Give your answer in the form $a + bi$.

steps.title: Multiply the brackets
steps.say: Expand $z_1 z_2$ term by term, as with any two brackets. Four products, then replace $i^2$ with $-1$.

steps.title: Subtract
steps.say: Subtract $\hl{2}{4 + 2i}$ from $\hl{1}{8 - i}$. Take care: the minus sign changes both terms in the bracket.

higher.tip: Expand the top line and the bottom line separately. Each is a step the marks are tied to.
Watch $i^2$. Mishandling $-2i^2$ is the usual lost mark.

ordinary.tip: Write out the substitution first, then distribute. Correct substitution on its own earns partial credit.
Show the multiplication line by line. Some correct multiplication is rewarded even if the final answer is wrong.
